basic_identification.full_title: Cycle and Rickshaw Pneumatic Tyres — Specification (Fourth Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Transport Engineering / Bicycles (approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Bicycles Sectional Committee under the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the dimensional, material, and physical performance requirements for pneumatic tyres used on bicycles (cycles) and cycle rickshaws. It applies to tyres mounted on straight side/wired-on rims or hooked bead rims, for both general-duty and heavy-duty applications, ensuring on-road safety and quality.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Cycle and Rickshaw Tyres and Tubes (Quality Control) Order, 2023' issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry / DPIIT, Government of India, all pneumatic cycle and rickshaw tyres manufactured, imported, or sold in India must conform to IS 2414:2005 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Non-certified products cannot be legally sold, traded, or distributed. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Every tyre must have the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) legibly embossed or molded on its sidewall.

Tyres must consist of a rubberised cord fabric casing enclosing two single or multiple steel wire bead rings, with a tread made of a suitable rubber compound, completely free from molding fins at the bead and crown.

The tyre must be mounted with a tube on a specified rim per IS 624, inflated to 3.26 kgf/cm² (320 kPa), and conditioned at room temperature for 24 hours. The pressure must be verified and readjusted to 320 kPa before measuring overall width and overall diameter.

Enforces strict limits on design and minimum section widths, overall diameters, and maximum service widths across size codes including: 40-559, 47-559, 50-559, 52-559, 54-559, 57-559, 47-507, 52-507, 57-507, 47-406, 50-406, 52-406, 57-406, 47-355, 52-355, 57-355, 47-305, 52-305, 57-305, 47-254, 52-254, and 57-254.

Dumbbell specimens (Type 1 of IS 3400 Part 1) stripped from tread or sidewall must be thermally aged at 70 ± 1°C for 7 days in an air oven per IS 3400 (Part 4) to verify retention of tensile strength and elongation at break.

Peel adhesion is tested on a 45 mm x 200 mm specimen on a tensile machine at a rate of 500 mm/min. The force required to peel the tread strip from the casing cords must not be less than 4.0 kgf (40 N / 25 mm width).

requirements.requirement_type: Tyre Performance Endurance Test (Annex D & Table 3)

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2414 : 2005 (Reaffirmed 2021) is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing pneumatic tyres for cycles (bicycles) and load-carrying cycle rickshaws. Under India's statutory Cycle and Rickshaw Tyres and Tubes Quality Control Order (QCO), all such tyres must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to certify their structural strength, burst resistance, and rubber compound durability. The standard divides tyres into Type A (Heavy-Duty for rickshaws) and Type B (Standard-Duty for bicycles) and establishes strict mechanical limits. This includes minimum breaking loads for welded steel bead wire joints, 48-hour rubber peel adhesion thresholds (min 40 N), thermal oven ageing at 70°C, and a demanding three-stage progressive load endurance test run at 24 km/h on testing drums to ensure rider safety and transport reliability.
